A_general.open_code_note: The official repository describes the managed MCP server and provides setup instructions, changelog, and client examples; it does not contain the hosted server implementation. Its commit is not evidence of the deployed server's code.
A_general.release_status: The core toolset is documented as the default; the server is described as under significant development.
other_official_servers: Datadog documents regional equivalents of the hosted MCP endpoint, including https://mcp.datadoghq.eu/v1/mcp, https://mcp.us3.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp, https://mcp.us5.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp, https://mcp.ap1.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp, https://mcp.ap2.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp, and https://mcp.uk1.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp.
Datadog distinguishes a separate local-only Code Security MCP Server for code scanning; it is not the hosted observability endpoint analyzed here.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The reviewed public pricing page lists Datadog product prices but does not state a separate MCP server charge. MCP call limits are published as fair-use limits, not as a per-call price.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Datadog product pricing is usage-based and varies by product and billing term. Examples on the official US pricing page include Infrastructure Pro at $15 per host/month billed annually or $18 month-to-month; APM at $31 per host/month billed annually or $36 month-to-month.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP documentation states a fair-use limit of 50 requests per 10 seconds and 100,000 monthly tool calls; limits may change and may be adjusted by Datadog support. Underlying Datadog products have separate prices.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Organization-wide MCP Access must be enabled. MCP Write Access controls write tools. Users need mcp_read or mcp_write plus underlying resource permissions. Organizations can restrict network access by IP allowlist. OAuth redirect URLs can be allow-listed in Organization Settings.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization administrator; individual access also depends on the user's role and resource permissions.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted server exposes tools organized into toolsets. With no toolsets parameter, core is the default. The tool reference publishes tool names, descriptions, permissions, and examples, but not complete input schemas. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 without authorization.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: MCP authorization specification referenced by Datadog; exact protocol version not found.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The supplied endpoint response was HTTP 401 with a WWW-Authenticate Bearer resource_metadata challenge naming https://mcp.datadoghq.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp. The supplied resource metadata advertises bearer header authorization and the authorization server https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp. The supplied authorization-server metadata reports oauth_version 2.1; authorization_code, refresh_token, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer grants; S256 PKCE required; registration endpoint https://app.datadoghq.com/api/v2/oauth2/register; token endpoint auth method none; and scope mcp_all. Token lifetime was not provided. Datadog documents revocation through Authorized Apps; existing access tokens can remain usable until expiry.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration is advertised. Raw supplied metadata: protected-resource documents returned HTTP 200 with bearer_methods_supported ["header"] and authorization_servers ["https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp"]. Authorization-server metadata returned HTTP 200 with issuer https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp, authorization_endpoint https://app.datadoghq.com/oauth2/v1/authorize, token_endpoint https://app.datadoghq.com/api/v2/oauth2/token, oauth_version 2.1, response_types_supported ["code"], grant_types_supported ["authorization_code","refresh_token","urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer"], authorization_grant_profiles_supported ["urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag"], scopes_supported ["mcp_all"], code_challenge_methods_supported ["S256"], pkce_required true, registration_endpoint https://app.datadoghq.com/api/v2/oauth2/register, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["none"]. The path-specific OpenID configuration returned HTTP 404. Datadog also documents API key/application key header-based alternatives.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official tool reference identifies read and write operations through tool descriptions and permissions, but the reviewed hosted docs do not publish MCP annotation fields such as readOnlyHint or destructiveHint. 2. Some operations require explicit confirmation or preview-before-apply; for example, the AP​​M service-remapping deletion requires explicit confirmation, governance write tools request approval of an exact change, and log configuration updates/deletes return a preview. This is documented behavior; the mechanism is not identified as MCP Elicitation. 3. OAuth scopes_supported is only mcp_all. Datadog also requires user role permissions, underlying resource permissions, organization-wide MCP Access, and (for writes) MCP Write Access. Standard Role users have MCP permissions by default. OAuth redirect URL allowlisting and access revocation are documented. 4. Tool selection supports toolsets and omit_tools; only core is the default, toolsets=all enables all generally available toolsets, and preview toolsets are excluded from that shorthand. Regional endpoints are documented. 5. Access follows the authenticated user's existing Datadog access controls; RBAC, Data Access Control, and log restriction queries can scope retrieved data. The server says it cannot access resources hidden from that user. 6. Fair-use caps: 50 requests/10 seconds and 100,000 monthly tool calls, subject to change. Responses may be truncated; most tools have max_tokens. Large traces may be truncated. 7. Docs describe tool-specific validation and correction, including clear argument/query-syntax errors; no universal unknown-argument policy was found. 8. Tool calls are recorded in Audit Trail with tool name, arguments, user identity, and MCP client; usage and session metrics are emitted. Usage collection includes interactions, errors, causes, identifiers, and context such as user prompts leading to MCP tool use, retained for 120 days. 9. The tool reference contains a feedback form invitation; the official repository changelog says submit_mcp_feedback was added to the core toolset. It is not in the current documented default core tool list visible in the official reference result reviewed for this inventory, so it is not added to actions.json. No upsell result text was found. 10. Datadog publishes external plugins and examples; no server-delivered skills tool was identified in the documented default core list. Tool descriptions include behavioral instructions, such as using aggregate tools for statistical analysis and not individual inspection. 11. No documented persistence of prior agent behavior altering future tool availability or results was found; the Assistant toolset can continue conversations using a conversation_id, but is not part of the default tool inventory. 12. The hosted server has separate toolsets and regional endpoints; the endpoint supports selectable toolsets. Code execution runs in a managed sandbox. 13. Core includes SQL-based log analysis and toolsets can add execute_code, which exposes a JavaScript SDK namespace for Datadog APIs. Documentation says code-execution runs using the user's identity and permissions; no evidence found that it bypasses the documented role controls.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The server exposes separately selectable toolsets, including preview and generally available sets, and supports region-specific hosted endpoints. Its default core list can be altered with toolsets and omit_tools. The documentation also describes a separately selectable Datadog-managed code execution sandbox.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted implementation and verbatim initialize/tool definitions are unavailable; the official public repository does not include the server implementation. No estimate inferred from catalogues.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The documentation lists broad Datadog product functionality, but does not provide a complete operation-by-operation comparison between UI/API actions and MCP tools. The endpoint inventory is limited by default toolset, permissions, organization settings, and omitted tools. REST API parameters were not treated as MCP parameters. Sources: https://docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server/tools/ ; https://docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server/setup/ ; https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The server says toolsets let clients use only needed tools to save context and recommends `toolsets=all` for clients that support tool search. It recommends querying relevant documentation or schema tools before some operations. These are client-facing recommendations; no universal enforcement is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Datadog states: “The MCP Server does not send your Datadog data to a third-party AI provider.” It says clients and their model determine what returned data goes to the AI provider. It also states that authenticated-user access controls apply, usage data is retained for 120 days, and tool calls are recorded in Audit Trail. The docs identify IP allowlisting, organization access switches, role permissions, and revocation controls.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Datadog says tool calls are recorded with MCP metadata and provides usage metrics for monitoring. It describes the server as HIPAA-eligible, while saying users are responsible for checking their connected AI tools' compliance. It says the server is not GovCloud compatible.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The documented authorization, organization switches, audit trail, usage metrics, and fair-use caps are described as platform behavior. The specific audit and data-handling claims are documentation evidence; the closed hosted implementation was not independently inspected. Tool-level behavioral recommendations are not shown to be enforced unless a tool-specific confirmation or validation rule is stated.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint returned HTTP 401 and provided no tools/list output; the action inventory therefore uses Datadog's official documentation for the endpoint host and the documented default core toolset.

The official repository changelog records that submit_mcp_feedback was added to the core toolset, while the current official tool reference result reviewed for the default core inventory did not show that tool. It is not included in actions.json because the current reference is the official tool-name source.

OAuth metadata lists only the scope mcp_all, while Datadog's setup docs describe finer-grained role permissions, organization access switches, and resource-level permissions. These appear to be additional authorization controls rather than OAuth scopes.
observations_for_research: The tool inventory is connection-configurable: toolsets select categories, omit_tools subtracts named tools, and organization settings and user permissions can hide write tools.
Datadog documents both tool-level operation confirmation and an organization-wide write-access control, separating per-action safeguards from a broader administrative switch.

Usage telemetry includes client identity, user identifiers, tool names, errors, arguments in Audit Trail, and context leading to tool use; documentation states a 120-day retention period for usage data.
